issues.description: validate_conda uses POSIX-only os.X_OK check that fails on Windows for conda.exe/bat
issues.detail: On Windows, os.access(path, os.X_OK) is unreliable and frequently returns False for legitimate .exe/.bat files. Combined with the '*.exe' filter, users on macOS/Linux selecting 'conda' (no extension) will be blocked twice: once by the filter, once by X_OK semantics. Recommend platform-aware checks.

issues.description: File filter '*.exe' wrongly excludes non-Windows conda binaries
issues.detail: The browse dialog filter is set to '*.exe', which is Windows-specific. On macOS/Linux, conda/mamba/micromamba executables have no extension, so the file picker will hide them by default, forcing users to switch to 'All files'. Filter should be platform-conditional.

issues.description: validate_conda substring match accepts unrelated executables containing 'conda'/'mamba'
issues.detail: Checking `any(tool in out.decode().lower() ...)` will accept any binary whose --version output happens to mention 'conda', 'mamba', or 'micromamba' (e.g., wrapper scripts, unrelated tools). Should anchor on a stricter pattern like a prefix match on the first token of --version output.

issues.description: Custom conda path used without validating it on load from config
issues.detail: kernelspec.argv reads `conda_path` directly when custom_conda is enabled and passes it to conda_version/downstream commands without re-running validate_conda or checking existence. If the user edits the config file or the binary is removed, a stale/invalid path silently flows into subprocess calls and produces opaque kernel-startup errors instead of the friendly preferences message.

issues.description: conda_group is never added when custom_conda is unchecked-and-empty, but path widget stays editable visually
issues.detail: `conda_path.setEnabled(self.get_option('custom_conda'))` disables the line edit but the QGroupBox title and browse button styling don't visibly indicate the disabled state strongly. Consider disabling the whole conda_group or the browse button as well for consistency with how other gated preferences in Spyder behave.

issues.description: edit.setFocus() after select_file may cause focus-jump regressions in other browsefile users
issues.detail: create_browsefile is shared across many preference pages. Unconditionally calling edit.setFocus() after a file is chosen changes focus behavior for every existing caller, which can interfere with validate_callback flows and surprise users who expect focus to remain on the browse button. Scope the change or document the intent.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful escape hatch for non-standard conda installs, and the wiring through confpage/kernelspec is mostly clean. Main concerns are cross-platform robustness in validate_conda (X_OK semantics, '*.exe' filter, substring matching of --version output) and the fact that the custom conda_path is trusted at kernel-launch time without re-validation. A couple of smaller UX nits around the shared create_browsefile focus change and group-level enable state are worth a second look but not blocking.
